199:## 6. Text values (SGF Text)
200:
201:Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.
202:
203:Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).
204:
205:For each consumed character `c`:
206:
207:| Input | Output |
208:|---|---|
209:| unescaped `]` | end of value |
210:| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
211:| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
212:| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
213:| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
214:| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
215:| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |
216:
217:There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.
218:
219:Order of checks after reading `c`:
220:
221:1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
222:2. `c == ']'` → stop.
223:3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
224:4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
225:5. else append `c`.
226:
227:EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).
228:
229:Examples:
230:
231:```
232:[\\]]           →  ]
233:[\\\\]          →  \
234:[[]             →  [
235:[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z
236:[a;b]           →  a;b
237:[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
238:[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
239:[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
240:[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)
241:[\\t = t]       →  t = t
242:```
243:
244:---
245:
246:## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)
247:
248:| Condition | Message |
249:|---|---|
250:| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |
251:| PropIdent present (or non-letter junk where a key/value should be) but no `[` | `"properties without delimiter"` |
252:| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |
253:
254:Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.
255:
256:Precedence:
257:
258:1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
259:2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
260:3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.

262:Public test (only one shipped here):

264:```python

266:```

269:
270:- `"()"` / `";"` → `"tree missing"`
271:- `"(;)"` → `SgfTree()`
272:- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`
273:- `"(;A[b]C[d])"` → two keys
274:- `"(;A)"` → `"properties without delimiter"`
275:- `"(;a[b])"` / `"(;Aa[b])"` → `"property must be in uppercase"`
276:- `"(;A[B];B[C])"` → parent + one child
277:- `"(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))"` → two sibling children
278:- `"(;A[b][c][d])"` → three values
279:- escapes / whitespace as §6

283:## 8. Edge cases
284:
285:- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).
286:- Only `\n` newlines; do not special-case `\r`.
287:- No spaces between `(`, `;`, keys, `[]`, `)`. Do not skip whitespace between tokens.
288:- `[` inside a value does not need escaping and does not start a new value.
289:- `)`, `(`, `;` inside a value do not need escaping and do not affect tree structure.
290:- Empty value `(;A[])` → `{"A": [""]}` (legal; may be untested).
291:- One node, no properties: `(;)`.
292:- Deep variation nesting: recurse; no explicit depth limit.
293:- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
294:- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.

# Implementation Guide: `sgf_parsing.py`

Do not change `SgfTree`’s public contract. Implement `parse(input_string) -> SgfTree`. Raise `ValueError` with the exact messages below. No optional whitespace, `\r`, charset, or non-Text value types appear in tests (README).

---

## 1. Public contract

```python
class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}   # dict[str, list[str]]
        self.children = children or []       # list[SgfTree]
```

Leave `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__init__` as-is.

`parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree`:

- One complete GameTree, consumed to EOF.
- `properties`: each key once; values are a list (order preserved, ≥1 entry per key).
- `children`: ordered; a linear Sequence is a linked list of single children; sibling GameTrees are sibling children.

Do not export parser internals.

---

## 2. Grammar (no inter-token whitespace)

```
Input      := GameTree EOF
GameTree   := '(' Node+ GameTree* ')'
Node       := ';' Property*
Property   := PropIdent PropValue+
PropIdent  := [A-Z]+
PropValue  := '[' ValueChar* ']'
ValueChar  := '\' AnyChar | <any except unescaped ']'>
```

Meaning:

- File is exactly one tree wrapped in `(` `)`.
- A tree must contain at least one node (`;`). `()` is invalid.
- A Sequence (`Node+`) is flattened into the `SgfTree` spine (see §4).
- Nested `GameTree`s after the Sequence are children of the **last** node in that Sequence.
- PropIdent is ASCII `A–Z` only. Any `a–z` in the ident → uppercase error.
- Every property has ≥1 `[value]`. Ident without `[` → delimiter error.

---

## 3. Data structures

Keep a single cursor over the input. Do not slice/copy the remainder on every step.

```python
class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, s: str):
        self.s = s
        self.i = 0     # next unconsumed index

    def eof(self) -> bool: ...
    def peek(self) -> str | None: ...   # None at EOF
    def next(self) -> str: ...          # consume one; error if EOF
    def expect(self, ch: str, msg: str) -> None:
        # if peek() != ch: raise ValueError(msg)
        # else consume
```

`SgfTree` instances: pass a fresh `dict` and mutate `.children` after construction, or build children first then pass them in. Never share one `list`/`dict` across nodes. `properties or {}` / `children or []` mean never pass `{}`/`[]` if you later mutate a default you don’t own — always pass a new object or assign after init.

---

## 4. Tree-shape algorithm

SGF `GameTree = '(' Sequence GameTree* ')'` with `Sequence = Node+`.

Map onto `SgfTree` as:

1. Parse the first `Node` → this tree’s `properties`.
2. Parse remaining Sequence nodes → a **chain**: each is the sole child of the previous.
3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

```
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [
       SgfTree({W:[ab]})
     ])
   ])
```

```
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))

nodes = [FF[4]]
variations = [B→W, B→W]
=> SgfTree({FF:[4]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [SgfTree({W:[ab]})]),
     SgfTree({B:[dd]}, [SgfTree({W:[ee]})]),
   ])
```

Mixed (handle even if untested):

```
(;A[B];C[D](;E[F])(;G[H]))
=> A → C → {E, G as siblings}
```

Pseudocode:

```python
def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect('(', "tree missing")
    if self.peek() != ';':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")

# Implementation Guide: `sgf_parsing.py`

Do not change `SgfTree`’s public contract. Implement `parse(input_string) -> SgfTree`. Raise `ValueError` with the exact messages below. No optional whitespace, `\r`, charset, or non-Text value types appear in tests (README).

---

## 1. Public contract

```python
class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}   # dict[str, list[str]]
        self.children = children or []       # list[SgfTree]
```

Leave `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__init__` as-is.

`parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree`:

- One complete GameTree, consumed to EOF.
- `properties`: each key once; values are a list (order preserved, ≥1 entry per key).
- `children`: ordered; a linear Sequence is a linked list of single children; sibling GameTrees are sibling children.

Do not export parser internals.

---

## 2. Grammar (no inter-token whitespace)

```
Input      := GameTree EOF
GameTree   := '(' Node+ GameTree* ')'
Node       := ';' Property*
Property   := PropIdent PropValue+
PropIdent  := [A-Z]+
PropValue  := '[' ValueChar* ']'
ValueChar  := '\' AnyChar | <any except unescaped ']'>
```

Meaning:

- File is exactly one tree wrapped in `(` `)`.
- A tree must contain at least one node (`;`). `()` is invalid.
- A Sequence (`Node+`) is flattened into the `SgfTree` spine (see §4).
- Nested `GameTree`s after the Sequence are children of the **last** node in that Sequence.
- PropIdent is ASCII `A–Z` only. Any `a–z` in the ident → uppercase error.
- Every property has ≥1 `[value]`. Ident without `[` → delimiter error.

---

## 3. Data structures

Keep a single cursor over the input. Do not slice/copy the remainder on every step.

```python
class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, s: str):
        self.s = s
        self.i = 0     # next unconsumed index

    def eof(self) -> bool: ...
    def peek(self) -> str | None: ...   # None at EOF
    def next(self) -> str: ...          # consume one; error if EOF
    def expect(self, ch: str, msg: str) -> None:
        # if peek() != ch: raise ValueError(msg)
        # else consume
```

`SgfTree` instances: pass a fresh `dict` and mutate `.children` after construction, or build children first then pass them in. Never share one `list`/`dict` across nodes. `properties or {}` / `children or []` mean never pass `{}`/`[]` if you later mutate a default you don’t own — always pass a new object or assign after init.

---

## 4. Tree-shape algorithm

SGF `GameTree = '(' Sequence GameTree* ')'` with `Sequence = Node+`.

Map onto `SgfTree` as:

1. Parse the first `Node` → this tree’s `properties`.
2. Parse remaining Sequence nodes → a **chain**: each is the sole child of the previous.
3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

```
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [
       SgfTree({W:[ab]})
     ])
   ])
```

```
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))

nodes = [FF[4]]
variations = [B→W, B→W]
=> SgfTree({FF:[4]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [SgfTree({W:[ab]})]),
     SgfTree({B:[dd]}, [SgfTree({W:[ee]})]),
   ])
```

Mixed (handle even if untested):

```
(;A[B];C[D](;E[F])(;G[H]))
=> A → C → {E, G as siblings}
```

Pseudocode:

```python
def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect('(', "tree missing")
    if self.peek() != ';':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")

    nodes = []
    while self.peek() == ';':
        nodes.append(self.parse_node())

    variations = []
    while self.peek() == '(':
        variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())

    self.expect(')', "tree missing")  # unclosed / wrong closer: ValueError

    for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
        a.children.append(b)
    nodes[-1].children.extend(variations)
    return nodes[0]
```

`parse()`:

```python
def parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree:
    p = _Parser(input_string)
    if p.peek() != '(':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # covers "", ";", "x", ...
    tree = p.parse_game_tree()
    if not p.eof():
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # trailing junk
    return tree
```

Empty string never enters `parse_game_tree`; public test requires `ValueError("tree missing")`.

---

## 5. Node and property parse

```python
def parse_node(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect(';', "tree missing")
    props = {}
    while True:
        c = self.peek()
        if c is None or c in ';()':
            break
        ident, values = self.parse_property()
        props[ident] = values
    return SgfTree(properties=props)
```

### PropIdent

Scan from current position:

- First char in `a–z` **or** any later `a–z` in a run of letters → `ValueError("property must be in uppercase")`. Prefer this over the delimiter error when both could apply (`(;a)`, `(;Aa)`).
- Consume a maximal run of ASCII `A–Z`. That is the key (length ≥ 1).
- If the first char is not a letter (`[`, digit, punctuation) → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`.
- After a valid ident, if `peek() != '[''` → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`  
  Examples: `(;A)`, `(;A;)`, `(;A(`.

Use `'A' <= c <= 'Z'` / `'a' <= c <= 'z'`, not `str.isupper()` (Unicode letters must not count as PropIdent).

### PropValue list

```python
values = []
while self.peek() == '[':
    values.append(self.parse_text_value())
# ident already guaranteed at least one '[' by the check above
```

`(;A[b][c][d])` → `{"A": ["b", "c", "d"]}`.

Duplicate keys in one node: last wins (not in tests; SGF forbids repeats).

---

## 6. Text values (SGF Text)

Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.

Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).

For each consumed character `c`:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| unescaped `]` | end of value |
| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |

There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.

Order of checks after reading `c`:

1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
2. `c == ']'` → stop.
3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
5. else append `c`.

EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).

Examples:

```
[\\]]           →  ]
[\\\\]          →  \
[[]             →  [
[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z
[a;b]           →  a;b
[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)
[\\t = t]       →  t = t
```

---

## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |
| PropIdent present (or non-letter junk where a key/value should be) but no `[` | `"properties without delimiter"` |
| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |

Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.

Precedence:

1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.

Public test (only one shipped here):

```python
parse("")  →  ValueError("tree missing")
```

Held-out cases expected from README + 2023-07-19 canonical set:

- `"()"` / `";"` → `"tree missing"`
- `"(;)"` → `SgfTree()`
- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`
- `"(;A[b]C[d])"` → two keys
- `"(;A)"` → `"properties without delimiter"`
- `"(;a[b])"` / `"(;Aa[b])"` → `"property must be in uppercase"`
- `"(;A[B];B[C])"` → parent + one child
- `"(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))"` → two sibling children
- `"(;A[b][c][d])"` → three values
- escapes / whitespace as §6

---

## 8. Edge cases

- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).
- Only `\n` newlines; do not special-case `\r`.
- No spaces between `(`, `;`, keys, `[]`, `)`. Do not skip whitespace between tokens.
- `[` inside a value does not need escaping and does not start a new value.
- `)`, `(`, `;` inside a value do not need escaping and do not affect tree structure.
- Empty value `(;A[])` → `{"A": [""]}` (legal; may be untested).
- One node, no properties: `(;)`.
- Deep variation nesting: recurse; no explicit depth limit.
- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.

---

## 9. File layout

Keep `SgfTree` at top unchanged.

---

## 1. Public contract

```python
class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}   # dict[str, list[str]]
        self.children = children or []       # list[SgfTree]
```

`parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree`:

- One complete GameTree, consumed to EOF.
- `properties`: each key once; values are a list (order preserved, ≥1 entry per key).
- `children`: ordered; a linear Sequence is a linked list of single children; sibling GameTrees are sibling children.

Do not export parser internals.

---

## 2. Grammar (no inter-token whitespace)

```
Input      := GameTree EOF
GameTree   := '(' Node+ GameTree* ')'
Node       := ';' Property*
Property   := PropIdent PropValue+
PropIdent  := [A-Z]+
PropValue  := '[' ValueChar* ']'
ValueChar  := '\' AnyChar | <any except unescaped ']'>
```

- File is exactly one tree wrapped in `(` `)`.
- A tree must contain at least one node (`;`). `()` is invalid.
- A Sequence (`Node+`) is flattened into the `SgfTree` spine (see §4).
- Nested `GameTree`s after the Sequence are children of the **last** node in that Sequence.
- PropIdent is ASCII `A–Z` only. Any `a–z` in the ident → uppercase error.
- Every property has ≥1 `[value]`. Ident without `[` → delimiter error.

---

## 3. Data structures

Keep a single cursor over the input. Do not slice/copy the remainder on every step.

```python
class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, s: str):
        self.s = s
        self.i = 0     # next unconsumed index

    def eof(self) -> bool: ...
    def peek(self) -> str | None: ...   # None at EOF
    def next(self) -> str: ...          # consume one; error if EOF
    def expect(self, ch: str, msg: str) -> None:
        # if peek() != ch: raise ValueError(msg)
        # else consume
```

`SgfTree` instances: pass a fresh `dict` and mutate `.children` after construction, or build children first then pass them in. Never share one `list`/`dict` across nodes. `properties or {}` / `children or []` mean never pass `{}`/`[]` if you later mutate a default you don’t own — always pass a new object or assign after init.

---

## 4. Tree-shape algorithm

SGF `GameTree = '(' Sequence GameTree* ')'` with `Sequence = Node+`.

Map onto `SgfTree` as:

1. Parse the first `Node` → this tree’s `properties`.
2. Parse remaining Sequence nodes → a **chain**: each is the sole child of the previous.
3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

```
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [

     ])
   ])
```

```
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))

nodes = [FF[4]]
variations = [B→W, B→W]
=> SgfTree({FF:[4]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [SgfTree({W:[ab]})]),
     SgfTree({B:[dd]}, [SgfTree({W:[ee]})]),
   ])
```

Mixed (handle even if untested):

```
(;A[B];C[D](;E[F])(;G[H]))
=> A → C → {E, G as siblings}
```

Pseudocode:

```python
def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect('(', "tree missing")
    if self.peek() != ';':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")

    nodes = []
    while self.peek() == ';':
        nodes.append(self.parse_node())

    variations = []
    while self.peek() == '(':
        variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())

    self.expect(')', "tree missing")  # unclosed / wrong closer: ValueError

    for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):

```python
def parse_node(self) -> SgfTree:

```python

while self.peek() == '[':
    values.append(self.parse_text_value())
# ident already guaranteed at least one '[' by the check above

`(;A[b][c][d])` → `{"A": ["b", "c", "d"]}`.

Duplicate keys in one node: last wins (not in tests; SGF forbids repeats).

## 6. Text values (SGF Text)

Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.

Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).

For each consumed character `c`:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| unescaped `]` | end of value |
| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |

There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.

Order of checks after reading `c`:

1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
2. `c == ']'` → stop.
3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
5. else append `c`.

EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).

Examples:

```
[\\]]           →  ]
[\\\\]          →  \
[[]             →  [
[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z
[a;b]           →  a;b
[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)
[\\t = t]       →  t = t
```

---

## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |
| PropIdent present (or non-letter junk where a key/value should be) but no `[` | `"properties without delimiter"` |
| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |

Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.

Precedence:

1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.

Public test (only one shipped here):

```python

```

- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`

---

- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).

3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

```
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [
       SgfTree({W:[ab]})
     ])
   ])
```

```
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))

nodes = [FF[4]]
variations = [B→W, B→W]
=> SgfTree({FF:[4]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [SgfTree({W:[ab]})]),
     SgfTree({B:[dd]}, [SgfTree({W:[ee]})]),
   ])
```

Mixed (handle even if untested):

```
(;A[B];C[D](;E[F])(;G[H]))
=> A → C → {E, G as siblings}
```

Pseudocode:

```python
def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect('(', "tree missing")
    if self.peek() != ';':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")

    nodes = []
    while self.peek() == ';':
        nodes.append(self.parse_node())

    variations = []
    while self.peek() == '(':
        variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())

    self.expect(')', "tree missing")  # unclosed / wrong closer: ValueError

    for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
        a.children.append(b)
    nodes[-1].children.extend(variations)
    return nodes[0]
```

`parse()`:

```python
def parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree:
    p = _Parser(input_string)
    if p.peek() != '(':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # covers "", ";", "x", ...
    tree = p.parse_game_tree()
    if not p.eof():
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # trailing junk
    return tree
```

Empty string never enters `parse_game_tree`; public test requires `ValueError("tree missing")`.

---

## 5. Node and property parse

```python
def parse_node(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect(';', "tree missing")
    props = {}
    while True:
        c = self.peek()
        if c is None or c in ';()':
            break
        ident, values = self.parse_property()
        props[ident] = values
    return SgfTree(properties=props)
```

### PropIdent

Scan from current position:

- First char in `a–z` **or** any later `a–z` in a run of letters → `ValueError("property must be in uppercase")`. Prefer this over the delimiter error when both could apply (`(;a)`, `(;Aa)`).
- Consume a maximal run of ASCII `A–Z`. That is the key (length ≥ 1).
- If the first char is not a letter (`[`, digit, punctuation) → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`.
- After a valid ident, if `peek() != '[''` → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`  
  Examples: `(;A)`, `(;A;)`, `(;A(`.

Use `'A' <= c <= 'Z'` / `'a' <= c <= 'z'`, not `str.isupper()` (Unicode letters must not count as PropIdent).

### PropValue list

```python
values = []
while self.peek() == '[':
    values.append(self.parse_text_value())
# ident already guaranteed at least one '[' by the check above
```

`(;A[b][c][d])` → `{"A": ["b", "c", "d"]}`.

Duplicate keys in one node: last wins (not in tests; SGF forbids repeats).

---

## 6. Text values (SGF Text)

Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.

Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).

For each consumed character `c`:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| unescaped `]` | end of value |
| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |

There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.

Order of checks after reading `c`:

1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
2. `c == ']'` → stop.
3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
5. else append `c`.

EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).

Examples:

```
[\\]]           →  ]
[\\\\]          →  \
[[]             →  [
[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z
[a;b]           →  a;b
[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)
[\\t = t]       →  t = t
```

---

## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |
| PropIdent present (or non-letter junk where a key/value should be) but no `[` | `"properties without delimiter"` |
| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |

Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.

Precedence:

1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.

Public test (only one shipped here):

```python
parse("")  →  ValueError("tree missing")
```

Held-out cases expected from README + 2023-07-19 canonical set:

- `"()"` / `";"` → `"tree missing"`
- `"(;)"` → `SgfTree()`
- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`
- `"(;A[b]C[d])"` → two keys
- `"(;A)"` → `"properties without delimiter"`
- `"(;a[b])"` / `"(;Aa[b])"` → `"property must be in uppercase"`
- `"(;A[B];B[C])"` → parent + one child
- `"(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))"` → two sibling children
- `"(;A[b][c][d])"` → three values
- escapes / whitespace as §6

---

## 8. Edge cases

- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).
- Only `\n` newlines; do not special-case `\r`.
- No spaces between `(`, `;`, keys, `[]`, `)`. Do not skip whitespace between tokens.
- `[` inside a value does not need escaping and does not start a new value.
- `)`, `(`, `;` inside a value do not need escaping and do not affect tree structure.
- Empty value `(;A[])` → `{"A": [""]}` (legal; may be untested).
- One node, no properties: `(;)`.
- Deep variation nesting: recurse; no explicit depth limit.
- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.

---

## 9. File layout

Keep `SgfTree` at top unchanged.
…

…
- Logging, regex-one-liners (escaping + nesting make a regex parser brittle; recursive descent is the intended design)

# Instructions

Parsing a Smart Game Format string.

[SGF][sgf] is a standard format for storing board game files, in particular go.

SGF is a fairly simple format. An SGF file usually contains a single
tree of nodes where each node is a property list. The property list
contains key value pairs, each key can only occur once but may have
multiple values.

The exercise will have you parse an SGF string and return a tree structure of properties.

An SGF file may look like this:

```text
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])
```

This is a tree with three nodes:

- The top level node has three properties: FF\[4\] (key = "FF", value
  = "4"), C\[root\](key = "C", value = "root") and SZ\[19\] (key =
  "SZ", value = "19"). (FF indicates the version of SGF, C is a
  comment and SZ is the size of the board.)
  - The top level node has a single child which has a single property:
    B\[aa\]. (Black plays on the point encoded as "aa", which is the
    1-1 point).
    - The B\[aa\] node has a single child which has a single property:
      W\[ab\].

As you can imagine an SGF file contains a lot of nodes with a single
child, which is why there's a shorthand for it.

SGF can encode variations of play. Go players do a lot of backtracking
in their reviews (let's try this, doesn't work, let's try that) and SGF
supports variations of play sequences. For example:

```text
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))
```

Here the root node has two variations. The first (which by convention
indicates what's actually played) is where black plays on 1-1. Black was
sent this file by his teacher who pointed out a more sensible play in
the second child of the root node: `B[dd]` (4-4 point, a very standard
opening to take the corner).

A key can have multiple values associated with it. For example:

```text
(;FF[4];AB[aa][ab][ba])
```

Here `AB` (add black) is used to add three black stones to the board.

All property values will be the [SGF Text type][sgf-text].
You don't need to implement any other value type.
Although you can read the [full documentation of the Text type][sgf-text], a summary of the important points is below:

- Newlines are removed if they come immediately after a `\`, otherwise they remain as newlines.
- All whitespace characters other than newline are converted to spaces.
- `\` is the escape character.
  Any non-whitespace character after `\` is inserted as-is.
  Any whitespace character after `\` follows the above rules.
  Note that SGF does **not** have escape sequences for whitespace characters such as `\t` or `\n`.

Be careful not to get confused between:

- The string as it is represented in a string literal in the tests
- The string that is passed to the SGF parser

Escape sequences in the string literals may have already been processed by the programming language's parser before they are passed to the SGF parser.

There are a few more complexities to SGF (and parsing in general), which
you can mostly ignore. You should assume that the input is encoded in
UTF-8, the tests won't contain a charset property, so don't worry about
that. Furthermore you may assume that all newlines are unix style (`\n`,
no `\r` or `\r\n` will be in the tests) and that no optional whitespace
between properties, nodes, etc will be in the tests.

[sgf]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Game_Format
[sgf-text]: https://www.red-bean.com/sgf/sgf4.html#text

# Instructions

Parsing a Smart Game Format string.

[SGF][sgf] is a standard format for storing board game files, in particular go.

SGF is a fairly simple format. An SGF file usually contains a single
tree of nodes where each node is a property list. The property list
contains key value pairs, each key can only occur once but may have
multiple values.

The exercise will have you parse an SGF string and return a tree structure of properties.

An SGF file may look like this:

```text
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])
```

This is a tree with three nodes:

- The top level node has three properties: FF\[4\] (key = "FF", value
  = "4"), C\[root\](key = "C", value = "root") and SZ\[19\] (key =
  "SZ", value = "19"). (FF indicates the version of SGF, C is a
  comment and SZ is the size of the board.)
  - The top level node has a single child which has a single property:
    B\[aa\]. (Black plays on the point encoded as "aa", which is the
    1-1 point).
    - The B\[aa\] node has a single child which has a single property:
      W\[ab\].

As you can imagine an SGF file contains a lot of nodes with a single
child, which is why there's a shorthand for it.

SGF can encode variations of play. Go players do a lot of backtracking
in their reviews (let's try this, doesn't work, let's try that) and SGF
supports variations of play sequences. For example:

```text
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))
```

Here the root node has two variations. The first (which by convention
indicates what's actually played) is where black plays on 1-1. Black was
sent this file by his teacher who pointed out a more sensible play in
the second child of the root node: `B[dd]` (4-4 point, a very standard
opening to take the corner).

A key can have multiple values associated with it. For example:

```text
(;FF[4];AB[aa][ab][ba])
```

Here `AB` (add black) is used to add three black stones to the board.

All property values will be the [SGF Text type][sgf-text].
You don't need to implement any other value type.
Although you can read the [full documentation of the Text type][sgf-text], a summary of the important points is below:

- Newlines are removed if they come immediately after a `\`, otherwise they remain as newlines.
- All whitespace characters other than newline are converted to spaces.
- `\` is the escape character.
  Any non-whitespace character after `\` is inserted as-is.
  Any whitespace character after `\` follows the above rules.
  Note that SGF does **not** have escape sequences for whitespace characters such as `\t` or `\n`.

Be careful not to get confused between:

- The string as it is represented in a string literal in the tests
- The string that is passed to the SGF parser

Escape sequences in the string literals may have already been processed by the programming language's parser before they are passed to the SGF parser.

There are a few more complexities to SGF (and parsing in general), which
you can mostly ignore. You should assume that the input is encoded in
UTF-8, the tests won't contain a charset property, so don't worry about
that. Furthermore you may assume that all newlines are unix style (`\n`,
no `\r` or `\r\n` will be in the tests) and that no optional whitespace
between properties, nodes, etc will be in the tests.

[sgf]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Game_Format
[sgf-text]: https://www.red-bean.com/sgf/sgf4.html#text

119:def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:

125:    while self.peek() == ';':

159:```python
160:def parse_node(self) -> SgfTree:
161:    self.expect(';', "tree missing")
162:    props = {}
163:    while True:
164:        c = self.peek()
165:        if c is None or c in ';()':

167:        ident, values = self.parse_property()
168:        props[ident] = values

172:### PropIdent
173:
174:Scan from current position:
175:
176:- First char in `a–z` **or** any later `a–z` in a run of letters → `ValueError("property must be in uppercase")`. Prefer this over the delimiter error when both could apply (`(;a)`, `(;Aa)`).
177:- Consume a maximal run of ASCII `A–Z`. That is the key (length ≥ 1).
178:- If the first char is not a letter (`[`, digit, punctuation) → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`.
179:- After a valid ident, if `peek() != '[''` → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`  
180:  Examples: `(;A)`, `(;A;)`, `(;A(`.
181:
182:Use `'A' <= c <= 'Z'` / `'a' <= c <= 'z'`, not `str.isupper()` (Unicode letters must not count as PropIdent).
183:

186:```python
187:values = []
188:while self.peek() == '[':
189:    values.append(self.parse_text_value())
190:# ident already guaranteed at least one '[' by the check above
191:```

193:`(;A[b][c][d])` → `{"A": ["b", "c", "d"]}`.
194:
195:Duplicate keys in one node: last wins (not in tests; SGF forbids repeats).

199:## 6. Text values (SGF Text)
200:
201:Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.
202:
203:Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).
204:
205:For each consumed character `c`:
206:
207:| Input | Output |
208:|---|---|
209:| unescaped `]` | end of value |
210:| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
211:| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
212:| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
213:| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
214:| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
215:| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |
216:
217:There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.
218:
219:Order of checks after reading `c`:
220:
221:1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
222:2. `c == ']'` → stop.
223:3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
224:4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
225:5. else append `c`.
226:
227:EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).
228:
229:Examples:
230:
231:```
232:[\\]]           →  ]
233:[\\\\]          →  \
234:[[]             →  [
235:[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z
236:[a;b]           →  a;b
237:[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
238:[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
239:[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
240:[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)
241:[\\t = t]       →  t = t
242:```
243:
244:---
245:
246:## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)
247:
248:| Condition | Message |
249:|---|---|
250:| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |
251:| PropIdent present (or non-letter junk where a key/value should be) but no `[` | `"properties without delimiter"` |
252:| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |
253:
254:Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.
255:
256:Precedence:
257:
258:1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
259:2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
260:3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.
261:
262:Public test (only one shipped here):
263:
264:```python
265:parse("")  →  ValueError("tree missing")
266:```
267:
268:Held-out cases expected from README + 2023-07-19 canonical set:
269:
270:- `"()"` / `";"` → `"tree missing"`
271:- `"(;)"` → `SgfTree()`
272:- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`
273:- `"(;A[b]C[d])"` → two keys
274:- `"(;A)"` → `"properties without delimiter"`
275:- `"(;a[b])"` / `"(;Aa[b])"` → `"property must be in uppercase"`
276:- `"(;A[B];B[C])"` → parent + one child
277:- `"(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))"` → two sibling children
278:- `"(;A[b][c][d])"` → three values
279:- escapes / whitespace as §6
280:
281:---
282:
283:## 8. Edge cases
284:
285:- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).
286:- Only `\n` newlines; do not special-case `\r`.
287:- No spaces between `(`, `;`, keys, `[]`, `)`. Do not skip whitespace between tokens.
288:- `[` inside a value does not need escaping and does not start a new value.
289:- `)`, `(`, `;` inside a value do not need escaping and do not affect tree structure.
290:- Empty value `(;A[])` → `{"A": [""]}` (legal; may be untested).
291:- One node, no properties: `(;)`.
292:- Deep variation nesting: recurse; no explicit depth limit.
293:- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
294:- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.
295:
296:---
297:
298:## 9. File layout
299:
300:Keep `SgfTree` at top unchanged.

# Implementation Guide: `sgf_parsing.py`

Do not change `SgfTree`’s public contract. Implement `parse(input_string) -> SgfTree`. Raise `ValueError` with the exact messages below. No optional whitespace, `\r`, charset, or non-Text value types appear in tests (README).

---

## 1. Public contract

```python
class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}   # dict[str, list[str]]
        self.children = children or []       # list[SgfTree]
```

Leave `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__init__` as-is.

`parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree`:

- One complete GameTree, consumed to EOF.
- `properties`: each key once; values are a list (order preserved, ≥1 entry per key).
- `children`: ordered; a linear Sequence is a linked list of single children; sibling GameTrees are sibling children.

Do not export parser internals.

---

## 2. Grammar (no inter-token whitespace)

```
Input      := GameTree EOF
GameTree   := '(' Node+ GameTree* ')'
Node       := ';' Property*
Property   := PropIdent PropValue+
PropIdent  := [A-Z]+
PropValue  := '[' ValueChar* ']'
ValueChar  := '\' AnyChar | <any except unescaped ']'>
```

Meaning:

- File is exactly one tree wrapped in `(` `)`.
- A tree must contain at least one node (`;`). `()` is invalid.
- A Sequence (`Node+`) is flattened into the `SgfTree` spine (see §4).
- Nested `GameTree`s after the Sequence are children of the **last** node in that Sequence.
- PropIdent is ASCII `A–Z` only. Any `a–z` in the ident → uppercase error.
- Every property has ≥1 `[value]`. Ident without `[` → delimiter error.

---

## 3. Data structures

Keep a single cursor over the input. Do not slice/copy the remainder on every step.

```python
class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, s: str):
        self.s = s
        self.i = 0     # next unconsumed index

    def eof(self) -> bool: ...
    def peek(self) -> str | None: ...   # None at EOF
    def next(self) -> str: ...          # consume one; error if EOF
    def expect(self, ch: str, msg: str) -> None:
        # if peek() != ch: raise ValueError(msg)
        # else consume
```

`SgfTree` instances: pass a fresh `dict` and mutate `.children` after construction, or build children first then pass them in. Never share one `list`/`dict` across nodes. `properties or {}` / `children or []` mean never pass `{}`/`[]` if you later mutate a default you don’t own — always pass a new object or assign after init.

---

## 4. Tree-shape algorithm

SGF `GameTree = '(' Sequence GameTree* ')'` with `Sequence = Node+`.

1. Parse the first `Node` → this tree’s `properties`.
2. Parse remaining Sequence nodes → a **chain**: each is the sole child of the previous.
3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [

     ])

```

```

        nodes.append(self.parse_node())

    variations = []
    while self.peek() == '(':
        variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())

    self.expect(')', "tree missing")  # unclosed / wrong closer: ValueError

|---|---|

2. `c == ']'` → stop.
3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).

5. else append `c`.

[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|

- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.

---

Keep `SgfTree` at top unchanged.

# Instructions

Parsing a Smart Game Format string.

[SGF][sgf] is a standard format for storing board game files, in particular go.

SGF is a fairly simple format. An SGF file usually contains a single
tree of nodes where each node is a property list. The property list
contains key value pairs, each key can only occur once but may have
multiple values.

The exercise will have you parse an SGF string and return a tree structure of properties.

An SGF file may look like this:

```text
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])
```

This is a tree with three nodes:

- The top level node has three properties: FF\[4\] (key = "FF", value
  = "4"), C\[root\](key = "C", value = "root") and SZ\[19\] (key =
  "SZ", value = "19"). (FF indicates the version of SGF, C is a
  comment and SZ is the size of the board.)
  - The top level node has a single child which has a single property:
    B\[aa\]. (Black plays on the point encoded as "aa", which is the
    1-1 point).
    - The B\[aa\] node has a single child which has a single property:
      W\[ab\].

As you can imagine an SGF file contains a lot of nodes with a single
child, which is why there's a shorthand for it.

SGF can encode variations of play. Go players do a lot of backtracking
in their reviews (let's try this, doesn't work, let's try that) and SGF
supports variations of play sequences. For example:

```text
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))
```

Here the root node has two variations. The first (which by convention
indicates what's actually played) is where black plays on 1-1. Black was
sent this file by his teacher who pointed out a more sensible play in
the second child of the root node: `B[dd]` (4-4 point, a very standard
opening to take the corner).

A key can have multiple values associated with it. For example:

```text
(;FF[4];AB[aa][ab][ba])
```

Here `AB` (add black) is used to add three black stones to the board.

All property values will be the [SGF Text type][sgf-text].
You don't need to implement any other value type.
Although you can read the [full documentation of the Text type][sgf-text], a summary of the important points is below:

- Newlines are removed if they come immediately after a `\`, otherwise they remain as newlines.
- All whitespace characters other than newline are converted to spaces.
- `\` is the escape character.
  Any non-whitespace character after `\` is inserted as-is.
  Any whitespace character after `\` follows the above rules.
  Note that SGF does **not** have escape sequences for whitespace characters such as `\t` or `\n`.

Be careful not to get confused between:

- The string as it is represented in a string literal in the tests
- The string that is passed to the SGF parser

Escape sequences in the string literals may have already been processed by the programming language's parser before they are passed to the SGF parser.

There are a few more complexities to SGF (and parsing in general), which
you can mostly ignore. You should assume that the input is encoded in
UTF-8, the tests won't contain a charset property, so don't worry about
that. Furthermore you may assume that all newlines are unix style (`\n`,
no `\r` or `\r\n` will be in the tests) and that no optional whitespace
between properties, nodes, etc will be in the tests.

[sgf]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Game_Format
[sgf-text]: https://www.red-bean.com/sgf/sgf4.html#text

+        self.expect("(", "tree missing")
+        if self.peek() != ";":
+            raise ValueError("tree missing")

+        nodes = []
+        while self.peek() == ";":

+    def parse_node(self):

+        while self.peek() not in (None, ";", "(", ")"):

+        return SgfTree(properties=properties)

+    def parse_property(self):
+        character = self.peek()
+        if not self._is_ascii_letter(character):
+            raise ValueError("properties without delimiter")

+        start = self.position
+        while self._is_ascii_letter(self.peek()):
+            character = self.next()
+            if "a" <= character <= "z":

+        name = self.input_string[start:self.position]
+        if self.peek() != "[":
+            raise ValueError("properties without delimiter")

+        values = []
+        while self.peek() == "[":
+            values.append(self.parse_text_value())

+    def parse_text_value(self):
+        self.expect("[", "tree missing")
+        value = []

+        while True:
+            character = self.next()
+            if character is None:
+                raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+            if character == "\\":
+                escaped = self.next()
+                if escaped is None:
+                    raise ValueError("tree missing")
+                if escaped == "\n":
+                    continue
+                if escaped.isspace():
+                    value.append(" ")
+                else:
+                    value.append(escaped)
+                continue

+            if character == "]":
+                return "".join(value)
+            if character == "\n":
+                value.append("\n")
+            elif character.isspace():
+                value.append(" ")
+            else:
+                value.append(character)

+        return (

+            and ("A" <= character <= "Z" or "a" <= character <= "z")

+class _Parser:
+    def __init__(self, input_string):
+        self.input_string = input_string
+        self.position = 0
+
+    def eof(self):
+        return self.position >= len(self.input_string)
+
+    def peek(self):
+        if self.eof():
+            return None
+        return self.input_string[self.position]
+
+    def next(self):
+        character = self.peek()
+        if character is not None:
+            self.position += 1
+        return character
+
+    def expect(self, expected, message):
+        if self.peek() != expected:
+            raise ValueError(message)
+        self.position += 1
+
+    def parse_game_tree(self):
+        self.expect("(", "tree missing")
+        if self.peek() != ";":
+            raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+        nodes = []
+        while self.peek() == ";":
+            nodes.append(self.parse_node())
+
+        variations = []
+        while self.peek() == "(":
+            variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())
+
+        self.expect(")", "tree missing")
+
+        for parent, child in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
+            parent.children.append(child)
+        nodes[-1].children.extend(variations)
+        return nodes[0]
+
+    def parse_node(self):
+        self.expect(";", "tree missing")
+        properties = {}
+
+        while self.peek() not in (None, ";", "(", ")"):
+            name, values = self.parse_property()
+            properties[name] = values
+
+        return SgfTree(properties=properties)
+
+    def parse_property(self):
+        character = self.peek()
+        if not self._is_ascii_letter(character):
+            raise ValueError("properties without delimiter")
+
+        start = self.position
+        while self._is_ascii_letter(self.peek()):
+            character = self.next()
+            if "a" <= character <= "z":
+                raise ValueError("property must be in uppercase")
+
+        name = self.input_string[start:self.position]
+        if self.peek() != "[":
+            raise ValueError("properties without delimiter")
+
+        values = []
+        while self.peek() == "[":
+            values.append(self.parse_text_value())
+        return name, values
+
+    def parse_text_value(self):
+        self.expect("[", "tree missing")
+        value = []
+
+        while True:
+            character = self.next()
+            if character is None:
+                raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+            if character == "\\":
+                escaped = self.next()
+                if escaped is None:
+                    raise ValueError("tree missing")
+                if escaped == "\n":
+                    continue
+                if escaped.isspace():
+                    value.append(" ")
+                else:
+                    value.append(escaped)
+                continue
+
+            if character == "]":
+                return "".join(value)
+            if character == "\n":
+                value.append("\n")
+            elif character.isspace():
+                value.append(" ")
+            else:
+                value.append(character)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _is_ascii_letter(character):
+        return (
+            character is not None
+            and ("A" <= character <= "Z" or "a" <= character <= "z")
+        )
+
+
+def parse(input_string):
+    parser = _Parser(input_string)
+    if parser.peek() != "(":
+        raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+    tree = parser.parse_game_tree()
+    if not parser.eof():
+        raise ValueError("tree missing")
+    return tree

+class _Parser:
+    def __init__(self, input_string):
+        self.input_string = input_string
+        self.position = 0
+
+    def eof(self):
+        return self.position >= len(self.input_string)
+
+    def peek(self):
+        if self.eof():
+            return None
+        return self.input_string[self.position]
+
+    def next(self):
+        character = self.peek()
+        if character is not None:
+            self.position += 1
+        return character
+
+    def expect(self, expected, message):
+        if self.peek() != expected:
+            raise ValueError(message)
+        self.position += 1
+
+    def parse_game_tree(self):
+        self.expect("(", "tree missing")
+        if self.peek() != ";":
+            raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+        nodes = []
+        while self.peek() == ";":
+            nodes.append(self.parse_node())
+
+        variations = []
+        while self.peek() == "(":
+            variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())
+
+        self.expect(")", "tree missing")
+
+        for parent, child in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
+            parent.children.append(child)
+        nodes[-1].children.extend(variations)
+        return nodes[0]
+
+    def parse_node(self):
+        self.expect(";", "tree missing")
+        properties = {}
+
+        while self.peek() not in (None, ";", "(", ")"):
+            name, values = self.parse_property()
+            properties[name] = values
+
+        return SgfTree(properties=properties)
+
+    def parse_property(self):
+        character = self.peek()
+        if not self._is_ascii_letter(character):
+            raise ValueError("properties without delimiter")
+
+        start = self.position
+        while self._is_ascii_letter(self.peek()):
+            character = self.next()
+            if "a" <= character <= "z":
+                raise ValueError("property must be in uppercase")
+
+        name = self.input_string[start:self.position]
+        if self.peek() != "[":
+            raise ValueError("properties without delimiter")
+
+        values = []
+        while self.peek() == "[":
+            values.append(self.parse_text_value())
+        return name, values
+
+    def parse_text_value(self):
+        self.expect("[", "tree missing")
+        value = []
+
+        while True:
+            character = self.next()
+            if character is None:
+                raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+            if character == "\\":
+                escaped = self.next()
+                if escaped is None:
+                    raise ValueError("tree missing")
+                if escaped == "\n":
+                    continue
+                if escaped.isspace():
+                    value.append(" ")
+                else:
+                    value.append(escaped)
+                continue
+
+            if character == "]":
+                return "".join(value)
+            if character == "\n":
+                value.append("\n")
+            elif character.isspace():
+                value.append(" ")
+            else:
+                value.append(character)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _is_ascii_letter(character):
+        return (
+            character is not None
+            and ("A" <= character <= "Z" or "a" <= character <= "z")
+        )
+
+
+def parse(input_string):
+    parser = _Parser(input_string)
+    if parser.peek() != "(":
+        raise ValueError("tree missing")
+
+    tree = parser.parse_game_tree()
+    if not parser.eof():
+        raise ValueError("tree missing")
+    return tree

# Implementation Guide: `sgf_parsing.py`
…
## 9. File layout
…
Keep `SgfTree` at top unchanged.

Replace `parse`:

1. `_Parser` (or nested functions + `nonlocal i`) in the same module.
2. `parse()` as the only extra public function.

Suggested methods: `parse_game_tree`, `parse_node`, `parse_property`, `parse_text_value`, plus `peek`/`next`/`expect`/`eof`.

Complexity: O(n) time, O(n) stack/output.

---

## 10. Verification

Run `python -m unittest public_test.py` (empty input).

Do not add tests, do not edit `sgf_parsing.py` in the planning step, do not fetch canonical-data or solutions.

Self-check before coding is done: mentally walk README samples and every row in §7 through the cursor machine.

---

## 11. Non-goals

- Collection of multiple top-level trees
- Optional whitespace, comments outside Text, charset
- Other SGF value types (Number, Point, …)
- Changing `SgfTree` equality or adding extra dunder methods
- Logging, regex-one-liners (escaping + nesting make a regex parser brittle; recursive descent is the intended design)

199:## 6. Text values (SGF Text)
200:
201:Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.
202:
203:Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).
204:
205:For each consumed character `c`:
206:
207:| Input | Output |
208:|---|---|
209:| unescaped `]` | end of value |
210:| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
211:| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
212:| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
213:| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
214:| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
215:| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |
216:
217:There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.
218:
219:Order of checks after reading `c`:
220:
221:1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
222:2. `c == ']'` → stop.
223:3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
224:4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
225:5. else append `c`.
226:
227:EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).
228:
229:Examples:
230:
231:```
232:[\\]]           →  ]
233:[\\\\]          →  \
234:[[]             →  [
235:[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z
236:[a;b]           →  a;b
237:[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
238:[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
239:[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
240:[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)
241:[\\t = t]       →  t = t
242:```
243:
244:---
245:
246:## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)
247:
248:| Condition | Message |
249:|---|---|
250:| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |
251:| PropIdent present (or non-letter junk where a key/value should be) but no `[` | `"properties without delimiter"` |
252:| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |
253:
254:Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.
255:
256:Precedence:
257:
258:1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
259:2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
260:3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.
261:
262:Public test (only one shipped here):

264:```python

266:```

268:Held-out cases expected from README + 2023-07-19 canonical set:
269:
270:- `"()"` / `";"` → `"tree missing"`
271:- `"(;)"` → `SgfTree()`
272:- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`
273:- `"(;A[b]C[d])"` → two keys
274:- `"(;A)"` → `"properties without delimiter"`
275:- `"(;a[b])"` / `"(;Aa[b])"` → `"property must be in uppercase"`
276:- `"(;A[B];B[C])"` → parent + one child
277:- `"(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))"` → two sibling children
278:- `"(;A[b][c][d])"` → three values
279:- escapes / whitespace as §6

283:## 8. Edge cases
284:
285:- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).
286:- Only `\n` newlines; do not special-case `\r`.
287:- No spaces between `(`, `;`, keys, `[]`, `)`. Do not skip whitespace between tokens.
288:- `[` inside a value does not need escaping and does not start a new value.
289:- `)`, `(`, `;` inside a value do not need escaping and do not affect tree structure.
290:- Empty value `(;A[])` → `{"A": [""]}` (legal; may be untested).
291:- One node, no properties: `(;)`.
292:- Deep variation nesting: recurse; no explicit depth limit.
293:- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
294:- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.

# Implementation Guide: `sgf_parsing.py`

Do not change `SgfTree`’s public contract. Implement `parse(input_string) -> SgfTree`. Raise `ValueError` with the exact messages below. No optional whitespace, `\r`, charset, or non-Text value types appear in tests (README).

---

## 1. Public contract

```python
class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}   # dict[str, list[str]]
        self.children = children or []       # list[SgfTree]
```

Leave `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__init__` as-is.

`parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree`:

- One complete GameTree, consumed to EOF.
- `properties`: each key once; values are a list (order preserved, ≥1 entry per key).
- `children`: ordered; a linear Sequence is a linked list of single children; sibling GameTrees are sibling children.

Do not export parser internals.

---

## 2. Grammar (no inter-token whitespace)

```
Input      := GameTree EOF
GameTree   := '(' Node+ GameTree* ')'
Node       := ';' Property*
Property   := PropIdent PropValue+
PropIdent  := [A-Z]+
PropValue  := '[' ValueChar* ']'
ValueChar  := '\' AnyChar | <any except unescaped ']'>
```

Meaning:

- File is exactly one tree wrapped in `(` `)`.
- A tree must contain at least one node (`;`). `()` is invalid.
- A Sequence (`Node+`) is flattened into the `SgfTree` spine (see §4).
- Nested `GameTree`s after the Sequence are children of the **last** node in that Sequence.
- PropIdent is ASCII `A–Z` only. Any `a–z` in the ident → uppercase error.
- Every property has ≥1 `[value]`. Ident without `[` → delimiter error.

---

## 3. Data structures

Keep a single cursor over the input. Do not slice/copy the remainder on every step.

```python
class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, s: str):
        self.s = s
        self.i = 0     # next unconsumed index

    def eof(self) -> bool: ...
    def peek(self) -> str | None: ...   # None at EOF
    def next(self) -> str: ...          # consume one; error if EOF
    def expect(self, ch: str, msg: str) -> None:
        # if peek() != ch: raise ValueError(msg)
        # else consume
```

`SgfTree` instances: pass a fresh `dict` and mutate `.children` after construction, or build children first then pass them in. Never share one `list`/`dict` across nodes. `properties or {}` / `children or []` mean never pass `{}`/`[]` if you later mutate a default you don’t own — always pass a new object or assign after init.

---

## 4. Tree-shape algorithm

SGF `GameTree = '(' Sequence GameTree* ')'` with `Sequence = Node+`.

Map onto `SgfTree` as:

1. Parse the first `Node` → this tree’s `properties`.
2. Parse remaining Sequence nodes → a **chain**: each is the sole child of the previous.
3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

```
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [
       SgfTree({W:[ab]})
     ])
   ])
```

```
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))

nodes = [FF[4]]
variations = [B→W, B→W]
=> SgfTree({FF:[4]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [SgfTree({W:[ab]})]),
     SgfTree({B:[dd]}, [SgfTree({W:[ee]})]),
   ])
```

Mixed (handle even if untested):

```
(;A[B];C[D](;E[F])(;G[H]))
=> A → C → {E, G as siblings}
```

Pseudocode:

```python
def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect('(', "tree missing")
    if self.peek() != ';':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")

    nodes = []
    while self.peek() == ';':
        nodes.append(self.parse_node())

    variations = []
    while self.peek() == '(':
        variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())

    self.expect(')', "tree missing")  # unclosed / wrong closer: ValueError

    for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
        a.children.append(b)
    nodes[-1].children.extend(variations)
    return nodes[0]
```

`parse()`:

```python
def parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree:
    p = _Parser(input_string)
    if p.peek() != '(':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # covers "", ";", "x", ...
    tree = p.parse_game_tree()
    if not p.eof():
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # trailing junk
    return tree
```

Empty string never enters `parse_game_tree`; public test requires `ValueError("tree missing")`.

---

## 5. Node and property parse

```python
def parse_node(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect(';', "tree missing")
    props = {}
    while True:
        c = self.peek()
        if c is None or c in ';()':
            break
        ident, values = self.parse_property()
        props[ident] = values
    return SgfTree(properties=props)
```

### PropIdent

Scan from current position:

- First char in `a–z` **or** any later `a–z` in a run of letters → `ValueError("property must be in uppercase")`. Prefer this over the delimiter error when both could apply (`(;a)`, `(;Aa)`).
- Consume a maximal run of ASCII `A–Z`. That is the key (length ≥ 1).
- If the first char is not a letter (`[`, digit, punctuation) → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`.
- After a valid ident, if `peek() != '[''` → `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`  
  Examples: `(;A)`, `(;A;)`, `(;A(`.

Use `'A' <= c <= 'Z'` / `'a' <= c <= 'z'`, not `str.isupper()` (Unicode letters must not count as PropIdent).

### PropValue list

```python
values = []
while self.peek() == '[':
    values.append(self.parse_text_value())
# ident already guaranteed at least one '[' by the check above
```

`(;A[b][c][d])` → `{"A": ["b", "c", "d"]}`.

Duplicate keys in one node: last wins (not in tests; SGF forbids repeats).

---

## 6. Text values (SGF Text)

Inside `[` … `]`, `\` is escape. Unescaped `]` ends the value.

Process **the actual characters** in `input_string`, not Python-literal escapes (those are already decoded before `parse`).

For each consumed character `c`:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| unescaped `]` | end of value |
| unescaped `\n` | keep `\n` |
| unescaped other whitespace (` `, `\t`, …) | `' '` |
| unescaped other char (incl. `(`, `)`, `;`, `[`, `\`) | as-is |
| `\` + `\n` | drop both (soft line break) |
| `\` + other whitespace | `' '` (same whitespace rule) |
| `\` + non-whitespace | that character as-is (`]`, `\`, `t`, `n`, `(`, …) |

There are **no** `\t` / `\n` escape sequences. Backslash + letter `t` → `t`; backslash + letter `n` → `n`.

Order of checks after reading `c`:

1. `c == '\\'` → must have a next char; apply the three escape rows.
2. `c == ']'` → stop.
3. `c == '\n'` → append newline (must precede `isspace()`).
4. `c.isspace()` → append `' '`.
5. else append `c`.

EOF before `]` → `ValueError` (message unspecified; any `ValueError` is fine).

```
[\\]]           →  ]
[\\\\]          →  \
[[]             →  [
[x(y)z]         →  x(y)z

[hello\tworld]  →  hello world          (real tab)
[hello\\\tworld]→  hello world          (backslash + real tab)
[hello\\\nworld]→  helloworld           (backslash + real newline)
[hello\nworld]  →  hello\nworld         (real newline kept)

```

---

## 7. Errors (exact `args[0]`)

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| `""`, `";"`, `"()"` , missing `(`, extra trailing input, unclosed tree when `(` was required | `"tree missing"` |

| Any `a–z` in a property name | `"property must be in uppercase"` |

Always `raise ValueError(msg)` so `type(err.exception) is ValueError`.

1. Not a `(`-wrapped tree with ≥1 node → `"tree missing"`.
2. While reading a name, lowercase letter → `"property must be in uppercase"`.
3. Name OK / missing `[` → `"properties without delimiter"`.

Public test (only one shipped here):

```python
parse("")  →  ValueError("tree missing")
```

- `"()"` / `";"` → `"tree missing"`
- `"(;)"` → `SgfTree()`
- `"(;A[B])"` → `{A:[B]}`
- `"(;A[b]C[d])"` → two keys
- `"(;A)"` → `"properties without delimiter"`
- `"(;a[b])"` / `"(;Aa[b])"` → `"property must be in uppercase"`
- `"(;A[B];B[C])"` → parent + one child
- `"(;A[B](;B[C])(;C[D]))"` → two sibling children
- `"(;A[b][c][d])"` → three values
- escapes / whitespace as §6

---

## 8. Edge cases

- UTF-8 in **values** is fine; copy through (after whitespace rules).
- Only `\n` newlines; do not special-case `\r`.
- No spaces between `(`, `;`, keys, `[]`, `)`. Do not skip whitespace between tokens.
- `[` inside a value does not need escaping and does not start a new value.
- `)`, `(`, `;` inside a value do not need escaping and do not affect tree structure.
- Empty value `(;A[])` → `{"A": [""]}` (legal; may be untested).
- One node, no properties: `(;)`.
- Deep variation nesting: recurse; no explicit depth limit.
- Parse must consume the whole string: `(;A[B])(;C[D])` is invalid trailing tree.
- Do not interpret FF/C/SZ/B/W/AB — keys and values are opaque after Text decoding.

---

## 9. File layout

Keep `SgfTree` at top unchanged.

---

```python

    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}   # dict[str, list[str]]
        self.children = children or []       # list[SgfTree]
```

Leave `__eq__` / `__ne__` / `__init__` as-is.

- One complete GameTree, consumed to EOF.
- `properties`: each key once; values are a list (order preserved, ≥1 entry per key).
- `children`: ordered; a linear Sequence is a linked list of single children; sibling GameTrees are sibling children.

Do not export parser internals.

---

## 2. Grammar (no inter-token whitespace)

```
Input      := GameTree EOF
GameTree   := '(' Node+ GameTree* ')'
Node       := ';' Property*
Property   := PropIdent PropValue+
PropIdent  := [A-Z]+
PropValue  := '[' ValueChar* ']'
ValueChar  := '\' AnyChar | <any except unescaped ']'>
```

Meaning:

- File is exactly one tree wrapped in `(` `)`.
- A tree must contain at least one node (`;`). `()` is invalid.
- A Sequence (`Node+`) is flattened into the `SgfTree` spine (see §4).
- Nested `GameTree`s after the Sequence are children of the **last** node in that Sequence.
- PropIdent is ASCII `A–Z` only. Any `a–z` in the ident → uppercase error.
- Every property has ≥1 `[value]`. Ident without `[` → delimiter error.

---

## 3. Data structures

Keep a single cursor over the input. Do not slice/copy the remainder on every step.

```python
class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, s: str):
        self.s = s
        self.i = 0     # next unconsumed index

    def eof(self) -> bool: ...
    def peek(self) -> str | None: ...   # None at EOF
    def next(self) -> str: ...          # consume one; error if EOF
    def expect(self, ch: str, msg: str) -> None:
        # if peek() != ch: raise ValueError(msg)
        # else consume
```

`SgfTree` instances: pass a fresh `dict` and mutate `.children` after construction, or build children first then pass them in. ---

SGF `GameTree = '(' Sequence GameTree* ')'` with `Sequence = Node+`.

Map onto `SgfTree` as:

1. Parse the first `Node` → this tree’s `properties`.
2. Parse remaining Sequence nodes → a **chain**: each is the sole child of the previous.
3. Parse following sibling `GameTree`s → **append** them to the **last** Sequence node’s `children`.
4. Consume `)`.

Worked:

```
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])

nodes = [FF/C/SZ, B[aa], W[ab]]
variations = []
=> SgfTree({FF:[4], C:[root], SZ:[19]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [
       SgfTree({W:[ab]})
     ])
   ])
```

```
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))

nodes = [FF[4]]
variations = [B→W, B→W]
=> SgfTree({FF:[4]}, [
     SgfTree({B:[aa]}, [SgfTree({W:[ab]})]),
     SgfTree({B:[dd]}, [SgfTree({W:[ee]})]),
   ])
```

Mixed (handle even if untested):

```
(;A[B];C[D](;E[F])(;G[H]))
=> A → C → {E, G as siblings}
```

Pseudocode:

```python
def parse_game_tree(self) -> SgfTree:
    self.expect('(', "tree missing")
    if self.peek() != ';':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")

    nodes = []
    while self.peek() == ';':
        nodes.append(self.parse_node())

    variations = []
    while self.peek() == '(':
        variations.append(self.parse_game_tree())

    self.expect(')', "tree missing")  # unclosed / wrong closer: ValueError

    for a, b in zip(nodes, nodes[1:]):
        a.children.append(b)
    nodes[-1].children.extend(variations)
    return nodes[0]
```

`parse()`:

```python
def parse(input_string: str) -> SgfTree:
    p = _Parser(input_string)
    if p.peek() != '(':
        raise ValueError("tree missing")   # covers "", ";", "x", ...
    tree = p.parse_game_tree()
    if not p.eof():

    return tree

def parse_node(self) -> SgfTree:

# Instructions

Parsing a Smart Game Format string.

[SGF][sgf] is a standard format for storing board game files, in particular go.

SGF is a fairly simple format. An SGF file usually contains a single
tree of nodes where each node is a property list. The property list
contains key value pairs, each key can only occur once but may have
multiple values.

The exercise will have you parse an SGF string and return a tree structure of properties.

An SGF file may look like this:

```text
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])
```

This is a tree with three nodes:

- The top level node has three properties: FF\[4\] (key = "FF", value
  = "4"), C\[root\](key = "C", value = "root") and SZ\[19\] (key =
  "SZ", value = "19"). (FF indicates the version of SGF, C is a
  comment and SZ is the size of the board.)
  - The top level node has a single child which has a single property:
    B\[aa\]. (Black plays on the point encoded as "aa", which is the
    1-1 point).
    - The B\[aa\] node has a single child which has a single property:
      W\[ab\].

As you can imagine an SGF file contains a lot of nodes with a single
child, which is why there's a shorthand for it.

SGF can encode variations of play. Go players do a lot of backtracking
in their reviews (let's try this, doesn't work, let's try that) and SGF
supports variations of play sequences. For example:

```text
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))
```

Here the root node has two variations. The first (which by convention
indicates what's actually played) is where black plays on 1-1. Black was
sent this file by his teacher who pointed out a more sensible play in
the second child of the root node: `B[dd]` (4-4 point, a very standard
opening to take the corner).

A key can have multiple values associated with it. For example:

```text
(;FF[4];AB[aa][ab][ba])
```

Here `AB` (add black) is used to add three black stones to the board.

All property values will be the [SGF Text type][sgf-text].
You don't need to implement any other value type.
Although you can read the [full documentation of the Text type][sgf-text], a summary of the important points is below:

- Newlines are removed if they come immediately after a `\`, otherwise they remain as newlines.
- All whitespace characters other than newline are converted to spaces.
- `\` is the escape character.
  Any non-whitespace character after `\` is inserted as-is.
  Any whitespace character after `\` follows the above rules.
  Note that SGF does **not** have escape sequences for whitespace characters such as `\t` or `\n`.

Be careful not to get confused between:

- The string as it is represented in a string literal in the tests
- The string that is passed to the SGF parser

Escape sequences in the string literals may have already been processed by the programming language's parser before they are passed to the SGF parser.

There are a few more complexities to SGF (and parsing in general), which
you can mostly ignore. You should assume that the input is encoded in
UTF-8, the tests won't contain a charset property, so don't worry about
that. Furthermore you may assume that all newlines are unix style (`\n`,
no `\r` or `\r\n` will be in the tests) and that no optional whitespace
between properties, nodes, etc will be in the tests.

[sgf]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Game_Format
[sgf-text]: https://www.red-bean.com/sgf/sgf4.html#text
